title: The Meeting Between Unequal Partners
title_ja: 対等ではないパートナーの会議
fact_notes: 人物・出来事・制度は架空の思考実験。実在の調査・統計・実証結果ではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: Suppose two fictional schools begin an international exchange project using a common online platform and a language that is not equally familiar to all participants.
sentences.ja: 架空の二校が共通オンライン基盤と全参加者が等しく慣れているわけではない言語を使って国際交流を始めるとしよう。

sentences.en: One school has extensive experience organizing international activities, whereas the other is participating in such a project for the first time.
sentences.ja: 一方は国際活動の企画経験が豊富で、他方は初参加である。

sentences.en: The teachers agree that the students should be treated as equal partners, and they initially interpret equality as providing every participant with the same speaking time.
sentences.ja: 教師たちは生徒を対等なパートナーとして扱うことに合意し、当初は平等を全員に同じ発言時間を与えることと解釈する。

sentences.en: During the first meeting, however, the students with greater experience introduce their proposals quickly, leaving some of the other participants uncertain about how they are expected to respond.
sentences.ja: しかし最初の会議で経験豊富な生徒は迅速に案を示し、他の参加者の一部はどう応答すべきか分からないままになる。

sentences.en: After the session, the teachers examine whether an identical allocation of time actually provided comparable opportunities for students to influence the direction of the project.
sentences.ja: 会議後教師は同じ時間配分が活動の方向に影響する同等の機会を実際に提供したか検討する。

sentences.en: Some students report that they needed time to understand unfamiliar expressions before they could formulate questions or identify alternatives to the proposals being discussed.
sentences.ja: 未知の表現を理解してから質問を作ったり議論中の案への別案を特定したりする時間が必要だったと報告する生徒もいる。

sentences.en: Others explain that they had interpreted the presentation of a detailed plan as an indication that the important decisions had already been made by their partners.
sentences.ja: 他の生徒は詳細計画の提示を重要な決定が既に交流相手によってなされた印と解釈していたと説明する。

sentences.en: The teachers therefore distinguish the formal opportunity to speak from the practical opportunity to participate in the process of deciding what the discussion is actually about.
sentences.ja: そこで形式的発言機会と議論の内容自体を決定する過程への実質的参加機会を区別する。

sentences.en: Before the next meeting, each school shares several preliminary suggestions in a short document using accessible language and clearly identifying questions that have not yet been resolved.
sentences.ja: 次の会議前に各校は理解しやすい言葉で未解決の問いを明示した短い文書に予備提案をいくつかまとめ共有する。

sentences.en: Students are encouraged to prepare alternative ideas in advance, and the teachers agree that proposals will not be considered final until both groups have had an opportunity to discuss them.
sentences.ja: 生徒は事前に別案を準備するよう促され、両グループが議論する機会を得るまでは案を最終決定と扱わないことに教師は合意する。

sentences.en: Rather than making one group responsible for presenting every topic, they arrange for the two schools to alternate the role of organizing and introducing the main discussion.
sentences.ja: 一方に全話題の提示を担わせず、中心議論の進行と導入の役割を二校が交互に担うよう調整する。

sentences.en: They also provide an additional written channel for participants whose contributions might be difficult to communicate within the limited time of a live conversation.
sentences.ja: リアルタイム会話の限られた時間内で意見を伝えにくい参加者のため追加の文章による経路も用意する。

sentences.en: The revised arrangement requires more preparation and does not automatically eliminate differences in experience or confidence among the students.
sentences.ja: 修正された仕組みにはより多くの準備が必要で、生徒間の経験や自信の差を自動的になくすわけではない。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, the teachers notice that proposals from both schools are now reflected more visibly in the questions selected for subsequent discussion.
sentences.ja: それでもその後の議論で選ぶ問いには両校の提案がより明確に反映されていることに気づく。

sentences.en: They avoid claiming that this observation establishes a universally effective model for international exchanges, since different groups may encounter quite different barriers to participation.
sentences.ja: 異なるグループには異なる参加障壁があり得るので、この観察が国際交流に普遍的に有効なモデルを確立すると主張しない。

sentences.en: Instead, they use the experience to identify specific assumptions about language, preparation, and decision-making that will need to be examined again as new participants join.
sentences.ja: 代わりに新たな参加者が加わる際に再検討する必要がある言語、準備、意思決定についての前提を特定する材料にする。

sentences.en: This hypothetical project illustrates why equal treatment cannot always be assessed solely by comparing the quantities of resources or time formally allocated to different participants.
sentences.ja: この仮想活動は平等な扱いを形式的に異なる参加者へ配分された資源や時間の量だけで常に評価できない理由を示す。

sentences.en: A common rule may have different practical consequences for people whose previous experiences and access to relevant information differ considerably.
sentences.ja: 共通の規則も過去の経験や関連情報へのアクセスが大きく異なる人に別の実際的結果をもたらし得る。

sentences.en: Addressing such differences does not require assuming that every participant from a particular school has the same needs or that all inequalities can be removed by a single procedure.
sentences.ja: こうした差への対応は特定校の全参加者に同じ必要があるとか一手順で全不平等をなくせると想定することを求めない。

sentences.en: The purpose is to create conditions in which the partners can contribute to the development of their shared activity rather than merely being present when its direction is announced.
sentences.ja: 目的は活動の方向が発表されるときに単に同席するのでなく、パートナーが共通活動の発展に貢献できる条件を作ることだ。

vocabulary.definition: thought of in a certain way
things added to a shared effort

options: Make experienced students lead every time.
Give everyone the same speaking time.
questions.explanation_ja: 発言時間を同じにする。

questions.prompt: Why did equal time not settle the issue?
options: Different levels of experience affected participation.
Both schools had exactly the same experience.
The platform could not show time.

questions.prompt: What did some students need before responding?
options: A final decision from the teacher.
Formal speaking opportunities versus meaningful participation in decisions.
questions.explanation_ja: 発言と意思決定への参加。

questions.prompt: What did both schools share in advance?
questions.explanation_ja: 予備案と未解決の問い。

options: The project failed to produce any proposals.
Different groups may face different barriers.
Ideas from both schools appeared more visibly in later questions.
A single school made every decision.
Experienced groups should always decide first.
Meaningful equality requires attention to practical conditions for participation.
questions.explanation_ja: 実質的な参加条件を考える。

grammar.focus: whether an identical allocation of time actually provided
until both groups have had an opportunity

paraphrases.source: One school has extensive experience organizing international activities, whereas the other is participating in such a project for the first time.
paraphrases.rewrite: One school is experienced in exchanges, while the other is new to them.

paraphrases.source: After the session, the teachers examine whether an identical allocation of time actually provided comparable opportunities for students to influence the direction of the project.
paraphrases.rewrite: Teachers asked if equal speaking time produced comparable chances to shape the project.

paraphrases.source: Students are encouraged to prepare alternative ideas in advance, and the teachers agree that proposals will not be considered final until both groups have had an opportunity to discuss them.
paraphrases.rewrite: No proposal would be final before both schools had discussed it.

paraphrases.source: A common rule may have different practical consequences for people whose previous experiences and access to relevant information differ considerably.
paraphrases.rewrite: The same rule can affect people differently when their backgrounds and information access differ.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 共通規則の異なる効果。
